title: Wire the MCP ecosystem
intro: Build the path from an LLM app to its data — two wires are forbidden, and both have names.
briefing: Route the host's need for context all the way to the data source. The inspector rejects any blueprint where the host hardwires the data directly (the M×N glue MCP exists to kill) — or where the client bypasses the server to reach a tool (clients speak protocol, not Python).

rules.label: The host contains an MCP client
The client holds a 1:1 protocol session with the server
The server exposes the tool with its schema
The tool actually touches the data source
No bespoke integration: the M×N glue MCP exists to kill
Clients speak protocol to servers, never to tools directly
Context can actually flow end to end

debrief: The chain — host → client → server → tool → data — is the M+N world: each side implements the protocol once, and the same server serves every MCP-compatible host. The first forbidden wire (host → data) is the old world: custom prompt logic, custom tool calls, custom data access, duplicated per app. The second (client → tool) is subtler: the client's vocabulary is ListTools and CallTool over a session — the server owns the functions, their schemas, and their execution. That separation is why a server built once is adopted everywhere.
